statement: Our neighborhood library offers free one-on-one digital help. Too many appointments go unused, so the branch manager wants to change the booking hours. Help us choose one small change to try over the next month.
hidden_brief:
[baseline] Two volunteers host 12 half-hour slots a week. Over four weeks, 16 of 48 slots went unused. Seven slots were never booked, six were confirmed bookings whose patrons did not show, and three were cancellations on the day with no replacement. The library has a paper waitlist with around five names per week.
[bottleneck] Six of the seven never-booked slots were near closing, but missed confirmed visits were not concentrated by time of day. Of six missed confirmed visits, five patrons later said they had called the wrong branch, written down the wrong date, or forgotten. The three same-day cancellations were recorded, but no one checked the waitlist.
[prior_attempt] In a two-week trial, staff made a short reminder call the day before. Four of six patrons reached confirmed or corrected their appointment, but one complained when a detailed voicemail disclosed the nature of the help. Staff did not track the overall effect on unused slots.
[constraints] No new software, staffing, or paid texts. The desk can spend about ten minutes on weekdays. Patrons can choose whether to be called and whether to allow a neutral voicemail; some have no reliable phone. Keep walk-in access and existing appointment hours for this pilot. The desk can use the paper waitlist if patrons opt in for short-notice calls.
[success] Over the next four weeks, aim for at least four fewer unused slots than the previous 16, with no privacy complaints and no reduction in access for people without a phone. Mark slots as unbooked, missed, cancelled, or refilled and track staff time. No comparison by individual patron is necessary.
known_good: Separate unbooked, missed and cancelled capacity; closing-hour availability looks relevant only to unbooked slots. A neutral opt-in confirmation or an opt-in waitlist refill procedure is defensible, but name the category addressed and whether the four-slot target is plausible. Do not claim the earlier calls proved a net benefit; use the privacy complaint to shape the plan. Keep a non-phone route and use the ten-minute staff budget. Compare the same categories over four weeks and define when to stop or adapt.
